notes.title: Isop0dyssey 1.2 Patch Notes + content farm & contest news
notes.content:
Hello! Patch 1.2 fixes the following:
[list]
[*]ending cutscene now has a prompt to skip
[*]the "unstuck" button no longer clips into the settings UI
[*]posters in the factory are now reading-friendly & no longer compressed into sub-atomic particles
[*]main menu cursor now works properly. (no need to restart the game anymore)
[/list]

that is all regarding the patch, but we have some other news:

New material will be added to our [url=https://www.youtube.com/@PARASITEPLAYHAUS]content farm on YouTube[/url] very soon about the residents of Abyss City.

Make sure you are in our [url=https://discord.com/invite/adAEsMW9rJ]discord server[/url] to be notified of our fanart contest with a 20 euro steam gift card prize! More info coming very soon. (There might also be a speedrunning contest!)

And lastly,
Some of us are making a silly little game about finding hidden isopods where you pan and zoom around a 2d world trying to find them all. You can help us populate the world by submitting your isopod drawings [url=https://forms.gle/V9WSTszpKsFUMNPb9]through the google forms link here![/url] submissions guidelines and some more info is available on the form itself.

Thank you for reading through the patch notes. You may now resume your shift.

notes.title: hotfix
notes.content:
this hotfix is mostly addressed to fix the issues encountered at the upper side district. (thank you bobtea on discord for reporting them!)

-player isopods will now be grounded instead of floating near Seliman Le Doux and Geracioti
-Geracioti's dialogue collision box is now much easier to interact with. They are now also solid matter
-a small house on the floor is no longer purple and has textures (we fixed this like 4 times but it keeps coming back. the house wants to be purple)
-Texture compression has been tweaked. a little better performance (question mark)

we are also investigating the other issues we found and that you have brought. We will continue with weekly patches and hotfixes as needed :3

Have a nice day!

notes.title: Isop0dyssey 1.1 Patch Notes!
notes.content:
hey everyone! First of all, thank you for playing Isop0dyssey! It's always magical to talk to you about your experiences exploring Abyss City & see gameplays (and even speedruns!) on YouTube.

isop0dyssey v1.1 fixes some bugs such as UI scaling issues, bad terrain geometry, trigger collision problems & quality of life improvements such as an "unstuck" button that you can find in the pause menu in case you get stuck somewhere or would like to be teleported to the nearest spawn point.

Achievements now fully work, and you now will have an easier time hunting down all the isopods to talk to through little markings on the minimap, as well as a... pirate map? on our Discord?!!?

Now everyone can “Get Back To Work” amongst other things.[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44079825/01f9f09df4deb33f9b1155d009d7724c1806d324.png[/img]

Don't forget to join our [url=https://discord.com/invite/adAEsMW9rJ]Discord Server[/url] to hang out with us & fellow isopod enjoyers! You can also report bugs there as well :3

Let us know what you think!

XOXO

notes.title: isop0dyssey: 12/01/24 devlog - the boss battle that is the racing soundtrack
notes.content:
Hello again! This is the first devlog of 2024. The factory line here has been chugging ever forward, and today I come to talk (and rant!) a bit about the sound design & some seaweed.

Firstly, the sound. This project has the most fun and most infuriating sound design challenges that I've had the pleasure to experience so far. It was not planned to be this way, but together with Likop we ended up using mostly self-recorded trash (staying true to Abyss City's values) like heavily processed tea slurping for isopod dialogue & old laptop fans for the sweeping hums of the soundtrack.

Whenever I start bumping a wall, reminding myself that we are supposed to have fun making games has helped me find fun solutions. This method has worked for most(!) of the sound design tasks where I could wrap up many things in the first or second try... but there is one track in particular that has defeated us many many times:

the racing music.

For the love of all detrivores, we have had so much trouble with this. Likop's solution has been classified as "psychological warfare" and is staying as backup in case we don't end up making it less repetitive, longer, or inflicted psychic damage.

I've scrapped more than 4 attempts, maybe 5th time is the charm. We shall see. I will hopefully return with happy news regarding the race track soon.

On other developments, Abyss City has recieved a fantastic layer of varnish from Nicole (our very own hired gun technical artist!), and she has done an amazing job glueing all the visuals together with her post-processing magic.

She also managed to implement the seaweed flora, but unfortunately we haven't yet figured out how to make them wave around. This might be down to us being locked into Unity's Standard Rendering Pipeline(it would be really nice if Unity can one day decide to stick with just one!). We will look into this if there is a good solution.

Until next time!
-maaruska
